                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>初始化:TRIGGER 时复位状态与全部输出(启动一次仿真)。
If the simulation is not running (TRIGGER = 0), set status to stopped and reset all calculated data
and status signals.

Set the previous time to the current CPU time (in readiness for the start of the simulation)

Set the OUTPUT, actual_Output and actual_PrevOutput to zero

If the simulation is not running, the block will terminate at this point.
▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄</Text>

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="2C" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="2D" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>运行状态:TRIGGER 保持→Running,记录开始/上次时间。
If the TRIGGER parameter has gone high, and is seen for the first time (status_Running = 0),
THEN a rising edge has been detected on the TRIGGER signal (the simulation has started).

If a rising edge is detected:
  1. Store the current time (actual_Time) as the simulation start time (actual_StartTime)
  2. Set the status_Running bit to match the TRIGGER signal
  3. Set the status_Stopped bit to match the inverse of the TRIGGER signal
  4. Set the actual_PrevTime to the actual_Time, i.e. actual_DeltaTime = 0 for 1st iteration
▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄
</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>

            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="2F" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>SIMULATION RUNNING — Check for TRIGGER rising edge</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
        </ObjectList>

                  <Text>运行时长:T_DIFF(现在-开始)。

The elapsed time is calculated in the LTIme format

                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>时长转秒(纳秒÷1E9)。
The wrkElapsedTime signal is of data type LTime (a 64-bit number representing the recorded
duration in nanoseconds).

This signal is converted first to a LInt (long integer) and then to a REAL number.

This REAL number is then divided by 1,000,000,000 (1×10^9) to convert the duration from 
nanoseconds to seconds

This final value is returned as actual_RunTime
▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄</Text>

                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
        </ObjectList>

                  <Text>步长:本次-上次时间差。

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="4A" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="4B" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>数值解:一阶离散递推 Output += (Input-Output)×dt/τ(带增益)——仿真器实时计算。
If the simulation is running and is in automatic mode, the following iterative, Real-time 
simulation calculation is carried out:

CALCULATION:
                              ΔT
   y[n] = Ka x[n]  ┼ (1-a) y[n-1]   where: a = ----------
                            τ+ΔT

Is rendered into the correct format as follows:


 cal_01 = ΔT             =  actual_DeltaTime

 cal_02 = τ + ΔT             = k_TimeConstant + cal_01

               ΔT
 cal_03 = a = ----------          = cal_01 ÷ cal_02
                τ+ΔT

 cal_04 = 1 - a             = 1 - cal_03


 cal_05 = Kax[n]            = k_Gain × cal_03 × INPUT

 cal_06 = (1-a) y[n-1]          = cal_04 × actual_PrevOutput


 OUTPUT  = Ka x[n]  ┼ (1-a) y[n-1]      = cal_05 × cal_06


▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>

                  <Text>SIMULATION RUNNING — Real-time simulation calculation</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
        </ObjectList>

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="4F" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="50" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>解析解:Output = k×Input×(1-exp(-t/τ))——精确阶跃响应,与数值解互验。
If the simulation is running and is in manual mode, the following discrete manual response to a 
step input calculation is carried out:


CALCULATION:

         ┌      -t/τ  ┐
   y(t) = KX│ 1 ─  e   │
         └       ┘


Is rendered into the correct format as follows:


 cal_01 =  -t/τ            = - 1 × actual_RunTime ÷  k_TimeConstant

         - t/τ
 cal_02 = ｅ              = EXP (cal_01)

               - t/τ
 cal_03 = 1 ─  ｅ              = 1 - cal_02


             ┌      -t/τ  ┐
 OUTPUT  = KX│ 1 ─  e   │       = k_Gain × INPUT × cal_03
             └       ┘

Note:    If k_TimeConstant = 0, cal_01 is set to the value k_NEG_MAX (the largest
     negative value available to a real number), preventing divide by zero errors.

▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
          <MultilingualText ID="51" CompositionName="Title">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="52" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>SIMULATION RUNNING — Over damped — Ancillary calculations</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
        </ObjectList>
      </SW.Blocks.CompileUnit>
      <SW.Blocks.CompileUnit ID="53" CompositionName="CompileUnits">
        <AttributeList>
          <NetworkSource><FlgNet xmlns="http://www.siemens.com/automation/Openness/SW/NetworkSource/FlgNet/v4">

                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>稳态判定:运行时间≥5τ → status_SteadyState(工程上认为进入稳态)。
Calculate the steady state time and set the status_SteadyState signal if the steady state time
has been reached



ANCILLARY CALCULATIONS:

 Time to 98% of steady state value (s) = 5τ              cal_TimeSteady
▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄</Text>

                  <Text>保存前值(供下一周期差分)。
The iterative nature of the calculation requires that the previous output and previous time are
updated at the end of the module, prior to the next iteration

The actual_PrevOutput is set to the current output (actual_Output) and the
actual_PrevTime is set to the current iteration time (actual_Time)

                  <Text>▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄  ＳＴＡＮＤＡＲＤ  ▄▄ 


TITLE:    DEBUG — SECOND ORDER RESPONSE SIMULATION


 

┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                          │
│          FC19512 — SOFTWARE MODULE DESIGN SPECIFICATION (SMDS)            │
│                                          │
│      The PDF version of the SMDS for this module is available online here:        │
│              https://psop.uk/pal-smds-fc19512-p               │
│                                          │
│      It is also available as part of the Project User Defined Documentation,      │
│      it can be accessed by selecting this module in the Project Tree          │
│      (on the left) and pressing SHIFT+F1                        │
│                                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────── ʷᴵᴰ⁻ᵇᵈᵖ ┘

FC19512_StdDebugInst2Order is a debug simulation subroutine.

The module simulates a second order process reaction in response to an input signal.

The simulation is adjustable in terms of the system gain, the frequency of oscillation (for those 
responses that have oscillating outputs) and the applied damping factor.

The output of the second order response simulation is in the form of a real number and is 
constrained to the resolution and range limits applicable to this number type within the 
Siemens Simatic S7-1500 controller.

The following second order responses can be simulated:

   1.  Over damped (slower response without oscillation)
   2.  Critically damped (fastest response without oscillation)
   3.  Under damped (oscillating with decreasing amplitude)
   4.  Undamped (oscillating system with constant amplitude)
   5.  Unstable under damped (oscillations of increasing amplitude)
   6.  Unstable over damped with unbounded, asymptotic rise (non-oscillating)

The module will simulate the 2nd order response according to the elapsed time since the 
module was activated.

The module also has a manual mode that can simulate an output at any specific time.

FC19512 is the 2nd Order Response Simulation module. The purpose of this module is to 
simulate a “second order” process reaction in response to an input signal.

Second order systems are the lowest order systems capable of an oscillatory response to a step 
input, such systems require two independent mechanisms for energy storage, for example an 
inert mass connected to a spring; a real-world example being the controlled damping of a car 
suspension system, the wheel representing the mass and the suspension system the spring, 
the control system would increase or decrease the applied damping to give the required 
response. Tuned mass damping of bridges and buildings are other examples.

Second order system can produce a range of responses depending on the damping 
configuration of the system. The typically quoted responses are:

Unstable system will either oscillate with increasing amplitude or increase asymptotically until 
the physical constraints of the system are reached.

Whilst second order systems are not as common as first order systems (see FC19511 and its 
associated calculation sheet), control systems are required to interface with them and hence 
a block to simulate them is a requirement of the PAL.



▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂
2.1      Scope and limitations of the simulation


The second order response simulation is able to simulate any of the following conditions:

   1.  Over damped (slow response without oscillation)
   2.  Critically damped (fastest response without oscillation)
   3.  Under damped (oscillating with decreasing amplitude)
   4.  Undamped (oscillating system with constant amplitude)
   5.  Unstable system with increasing oscillations
   6.  Unstable system with unbounded rise (non-oscillating) 

The simulation is adjustable in terms of the fundamental constants of a 2nd order system: 
system gain (K), natural frequency of oscillation (ω) and the applied damping factor (ζ).



▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁
2.1.1     The limitations of the simulation


The output of the second order response simulation will be in the form of a real number and will 
be constrained to the limits applicable to this number type within the Siemens controller.

The S7-1500 range of Controllers supports real numbers as values, these are 32-bit numbers 
and, within a Controller, have the following range limits:


 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
             LOWER RANGE LIMIT     UPPER RANGE LIMIT
 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
 S7-1500 real number:     ±3.402323×10^(-38)           ±3.402323×10^(+38)
 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――

It should be noted that with unstable responses, the result of any calculation will be constrained 
by the above limits; and, these limits may be reached very quickly.



▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁
2.1.2     The nature of the simulation calculations


The module will generate the correct responses for the six conditions listed in the previous 
section (§ 2.1). The responses for each of these conditions is specified in the associated 
calculations sheet [Ref. 101], available here:

         https://psop.uk/pal-calc-fc19512-p

These calculations are based around the mathematical functions available to the Controller 
(these are in addition to the standard mathematical operations: addition, subtraction, 
multiplication and division).

Each Controller supports the following common mathematical functions:


 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
 OPERATION    EXAMPLE         DESCRIPTION
 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
 SQR        x^2          Form the square
 SQRT         √x            Form the square root
 EXP        e^x          Exponential
 LN          log_e(⁡x)        Natural logarithm
 SIN         sin(⁡x)         Sine
 ASIN          sin^-1(x)          Arcsine, inverse sine
 COS          cos(⁡x)        Cosine
 ACOS        cos^-1(x)         Arccosine, inverse cosine
 TAN           tan(⁡x)         Tangent
 ATAN         tan^-1(x)         Arctangent, inverse tangent
 ABS        |x|            Modulus
 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
 Table 2.1 S7 Controller — common mathematical functions



▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁
2.1.3     A note on Laplace transforms


The interpretation of the time domain response of a second order system, is complex in nature 
and makes extensive use of the mathematical Laplace transform; this is a mechanism that 
allows ordinary differential equation to be manipulated algebraically; it replaces functions of 
time with a complex variable denoted by the symbol s, where s represents the complex 
number σ+jω.

The calculation sheet associated with this module [Ref. 101], explains the Laplace transform 
mechanisms and how they are used within the calculations necessary for the functioning of this 
module. Further explanation of the Laplace transform is not given in this document, again the 
reader is referred to the calculation sheet [Ref. 101].



▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂
2.2      The second order response


The response of a second order system (y) to an input (x) is defined using the general form of a 
second order system transfer function, this is expressed below in the time domain as a second 
order differential equation (see the calculation sheet [Ref. 101], Appendix B for details):

 d²y                dy
 ------  ┼  2ζω ----- ┼  ω²y  =  Kω² x
 dt²                dt

Where:    K is the system gain
     ω is the natural frequency of the system (rad/s)
     ζ is the damping factor

Applying the Laplace transforms for derivatives (see  the calculation sheet 
[Ref. 101], Appendix A for details) gives a frequency domain equivalent of:


 s²y(s) ┼  2ζωsy(s) ┼  ω²y(s)  =  Kω² x(s)

The transfer function is defined as the output divided by the input, in this case:

 y(s)                 Kω²
 ------- = --------------------------------
 x(s)      s² ┼  2ζωs ┼  ω²

The denominator of this equation, when equated with zero is referred to as the characteristic 
equation and in the case of a second order system it is a quadratic equation:

 s² ┼  2ζωs ┼  ω² = 0

This can be expressed in the form (see the calculation sheet [Ref. 101], Appendix A for details):

 (s ─ α )(s ─ β ) = 0

Where α and β are the roots of the equation, these can be determined using the standard 
solution for a quadratic equation (see the calculation sheet [Ref. 101], Appendix C for 
details), and are:


 α = ─ζω ┼ ω √(ζ²-1)

 β = ─ζω ─ ω √(ζ²-1)

In the case of a second order system, the nature of the response depends upon the values 
of the roots of the characteristic equation (α and β).

There are several possible responses and all are dependent on the damping factor (ζ):


 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
 DAMPING FACTOR (ζ)  ROOTS (α and β)          DESCRIPTION OF RESPONSE
 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
 ζ &gt; 1         Unique negative real roots      Under damped, slow response 
                           no overshoot

 ζ = 1            Coincident negative real roots  Critically damped, fastest response 
                           without overshoot

 0 &lt; ζ &lt; 1         Complex conjugate,      Under damped, overshoot with 
            negative real part          decreasing oscillations	

 ζ = 0            Zero real part,          Undamped, oscillates with 
            imaginary part ±jω         frequency ω

 −1 &lt; ζ &lt; 0          Complex conjugate,      Unstable, oscillations of increasing 
            positive real part        amplitude

 ζ ≤ −1          Unique positive real roots    Unstable, unbounded asymptotic 
                           increase
 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
 Table 2.2 Second order system responses to changes in damping factor (ζ)


To give some indication of how these responses are dependent on the α and β root values 
(either real or as complex conjugates), it is possible to plot these roots in an s plane diagram, this 
uses the base equation of the s value (see the calculation sheet [Ref. 101], Appendix A for 
details): 

 s = σ ┼ jω

The s plane plots the complex conjugates for the α and β root values on an x-y graph where the 
x-axis represents the real component (σ) and the y-axis the imaginary component (jω).

                  <Text>▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂
2.3      The calculations


The calculations needed to produce the second order system responses listed in Table 2.2 are 
all produced in the associated calculation sheet [Ref. 101]. 

There are six possible solutions to the second order system response and all are dependent on 
the damping factor ζ (see [Ref. 101], Section 6 for details). The final calculations are reproduced 
below and are shown in descending value of the damping factor ζ.

An accompanying spreadsheet [Ref. 102] is available, this allows all the various responses to be 
graphically simulated with adjustable values (it was this spreadsheet that was used to produce 
the various response plots used within this description).

The following sections show each of the six possible responses:

   1.  Over damped (slow response without oscillation)
   2.  Critically damped (fastest response without oscillation)
   3.  Under damped (oscillating with decreasing amplitude)
   4.  Undamped (oscillating system with constant amplitude)
   5.  Unstable system with increasing oscillations
   6.  Unstable system with unbounded rise (non-oscillating) 

For the stable responses, the output is generated for a step input x(t) = 1. The calculations also 
generate a good approximation for a ramp input x(t) = t and to a lesser extent, adequate 
responses for sinusoidal functions: x(t) = cos (t) or sin (t).

The ramp and sinusoidal response for unstable systems, are, in effect, identical to the step input, 
the nature of the input value rapidly becoming negligible compared to the unstable output values.

Note:    In the following sections, where ζ is a negative number, the expression | ζ | refers to 
     the magnitude of the damping constant, i.e. if ζ = –2 then | ζ | = 2.

═══ ANCILLARY CALCULATIONS:    ═══════════════════════════


There are no ancillary calculations for this response.

Note:    The magnitude of oscillation increases exponentially and is constrained only by the

     i.e. unstable system reach the computing limits of the system very quickly.

2.4      Operating modes


The block supports two modes of operation:

   •   Automatic mode:
     The module automatically calculates the elapsed time since the simulation started 
     and generates the appropriate output value

   •   Manual mode:
     The current elapsed time is supplied manually to the module; the module will then 
     calculate the output value based on this manual time value

3.1      The primary simulation signals


The simulation is based upon various signals passed to the module and the elapsed time since 
the simulation started:

 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
 SIGNAL         FUNCTION               RANGE       ACCESSED VIA
 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
 INPUT         The INPUT parameter is the x value    Unrestricted     Parameter 
           in the calculations of § 2.3
	
 OUTPUT        The OUTPUT parameter is the y value   Unrestricted     Parameter 
           in the calculations of § 2.3

 TRIGGER        The TRIGGER parameter activates      0 or 1     Parameter
           the simulation

 k_Gain          The system gain (K) term         Unrestricted     UT39512
           in the calculations of § 2.3       typ. 1-10

 k_NatFreq       The natural frequency of the system     +ve number      UT39512
           (ω) term in the calculations of § 2.3.     typ. 1-100
           In units of radians/second (rad/s)

 k_DampFactor     The damping factor of the system      Unrestricted     UT39512
           (ζ) in the calculations of § 2.3 

           The damping factor determines the type of response:
           ζ &gt; 1        Stable over damped (no oscillations)
           ζ = 1     Stable critically damped (no oscillations)
           0 &lt; ζ &lt; 1  Stable under damped (decaying oscillations)
           ζ = 0     Stable undamped (constant oscillations)
           -1 &lt; ζ &lt; 0 Unstable under damped (inc. oscillations)
           ζ ≤ -1       Unstable over damped (asymptotic increase)

 cal_DampFreqRS   Damped (actual) frequency of      +ve number      UT39512
           the system (rad/s).           calculated by
           Ω in the calculations of § 2.3      the module

 actual_StartTime   The CPU time when the simulation    DTL value    UT39512
           started (rising edge of TRIGGER)      of RTC

 actual_RunTime     The elapsed time (t) term           +ve number      UT39512
           in the calculations of § 2.3.         calculated by
           Always measured in seconds       the module
           Current CPU time - actual_StartTime
 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――


The most important of these terms is the damping factor (k_DampFactor), this determines the 
type of response (stable, unstable, oscillating, exponential &amp;c.) and also the speed of the 
response, the smaller the damping factor, the faster the system will reach the steady state 
value (in the case where k_DampFactor is between zero and one, the steady state value will 
be reached quickly, but there will be some degree of overshoot, see the figures of § 2.3).

The natural frequency (k_NatFreq), determines the frequency of oscillation for those responses 
that oscillate (oscillations occur when –1 &lt; k_DampFactor &lt; +1). For non-oscillating responses, 
the larger the natural frequency, the quicker the response.

The system gain (k_Gain), is simply a common multiplier that amplifies the output response. 
By default the system gain is set to a value of one (i.e. unity gain). If the system gain k_Gain 
is set zero, the OUTPUT will be zero under all circumstances

The elapsed time actual_RunTime is calculated from the real time clock within the CPU. On the 
rising edge of the TRIGGER parameter, the CPU real time clock is read and the value stored in 
the variable actual_StartTime, on each subsequent call to the block, the real time clock is 
once again read and the actual_StartTime value is subtracted from this value to give the 
current elapsed time, this is converted to seconds and is stored as the actual_RunTime value.

The TRIGGER signal is simply used to start and stop the simulation. A rising edge on the TRIGGER 
signal causes the current CPU time to be stored (actual_StartTime) and sets the elapsed time 
to zero (actual_RunTime). The simulation will run whilever the TRIGGER signal is high (has a
 value of 1), each time the module is called, the elapsed time (actual_RunTime) is updated 
(see the previous paragraph) and the output calculated accordingly.

If the TRIGGER signal is low (0), the simulation is instantly stopped and the OUTPUT parameter 
is set to zero.

3.2      The response calculation


The calculation that is performed by the module is entirely dependent on the k_DampFactor 
(referred to as ζ, the Greek letter Zeta, in the following equations).

The calculations given in section 2.3 (and summarised below) use Greek characters for the 
main variables, the calculations use various parameters and UDT variables that have plain
English names, The association between these variables and the Greek nomenclature is given
below.

――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
ζ &gt; 1        STABLE     over damped (no oscillations)       Equation (2.1)

        ╓   1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t       1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t ╖
y = x K║1 ─ -- │------------------ ┼ 1│ｅ         ┼ -- │------------------ ─ 1│ｅ           ║
     ╙   2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            ╜
――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
ζ = 1     STABLE     critically damped (no oscillations)      Equation (2.2)

      ╓       - ωt  ╖
 y = x K║1 ─ (1 ┼ ωt) ｅ    ║
      ╙            ╜
――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
0 &lt; ζ &lt; 1  STABLE     under damped (decaying oscillations)     Equation (2.3)

      ╓      - ζω t  ┌        ζ            ┐╖
 y = x K║1 ─ ｅ   │COS (Ωt) ┼ ------------------ SIN (Ωt)│║  where Ω =  ω √(1 ─ ζ²)
      ╙       └       √(1 ─ ζ²)       ┘╜
――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
ζ = 0     STABLE     undamped (constant oscillations)      Equation (2.4)

      ╓       ╖
 y = x K║1 ─ COS (ωt) ║
      ╙       ╜
――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
-1 &lt; ζ &lt; 0 UNSTABLE   under damped (inc. oscillations)         Equation (2.5)

      ╓      - ζω t  ┌        ζ            ┐╖
 y = x K║1 ─ ｅ   │COS (Ωt) ┼ ------------------ SIN (Ωt)│║  where Ω =  ω √(1 ─ ζ²)
      ╙       └       √(1 ─ ζ²)       ┘╜
――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
ζ ≤ -1       UNSTABLE   over damped (asymptotic increase)      Equation (2.6)

        ╓   1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t       1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t ╖
y = x K║1 ─ -- │------------------ ┼ 1│ｅ         ┼ -- │------------------ ─ 1│ｅ           ║

――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――

Where:    x is the input signal,       parameter INPUT
     y is the output response,    parameter OUTPUT
     K   is the system gain    k_Gain
     ζ is the damping factor    k_DampFactor
     ω   is the natural frequency   k_NatFreq
     Ω   is the damped frequency cal_DampFreqRS
     t    is the elapsed time     actual_RunTime

The module will determine which calculation to perform based entirely on the value of the 
damping factor k_DampFactor (Greek symbol ζ) as shown above.

Each of these calculations, while being somewhat complicated and convoluted, can all be 
accommodated with the mathematical functions available to a Siemens Controller, see § 3.5.

The status_Running and status_Stopped are determined purely by the status of the TRIGGER 
parameter, if this is set high (1), status_Running will be high and status_Stopped low. If  TRIGGER 
parameter, if this is set low (0), status_Running will be low and status_Stopped high. The 
status_Running and status_Stopped signals are always the inverse of each other.	 

The six simulation response type signals are mutually exclusive, only one will be active if the 
simulation is running. Whichever is active, is determined by the k_DampFactor (ζ in the equations) 
as follows:


 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
 SIGNAL          FUNCTION         OSCILLATING   STABLE
 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
 status_OverDamp     k_DampFactor &gt; 1      NO        YES
 status_CritDamp     k_DampFactor = 1      NO        YES
 status_UnderDamp   0 &lt; k_DampFactor &lt; 1   YES       YES
 status_Undamped     k_DampFactor = 0      YES       YES
 status_USUnder      –1 &lt; k_DampFactor &lt; 0      YES       NO
 status_USOver     k_DampFactor ≤ –1      NO        NO
 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――


If the response is stable (k_DampFactor ≥ 0), status_Stable is set high (1), if the response is 
unstable (k_DampFactor &lt; 0), status_Stable is set low (0).

If the response is stable (k_DampFactor ≥ 0), the status_SteadyState signal will be activated 
when the OUTPUT is within ±2% of the steady state value and remains within this tolerance 
(i.e. for the underdamped oscillatory response, the status_SteadyState signal will not activate
until the oscillations have decayed to the point at which they remain within  the ±2% of steady 
state value).

The module also produces some additional, informational, signals:

                              0 = non-oscillating response

                oscillation in radians per  
                second (ω or Ω in § 3.2)

 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――

 
If the response is oscillatory in nature (e.g. –1 &lt; k_DampFactor &lt; 1), the status_Osc signal will be 
set high (1), if the response is non-oscillatory in nature, status_Osc signal will be set low (0).

For oscillatory responses, the actual frequency of the oscillation is specified in radians per  
second in the signal status_OscFreqRS, and in Hertz in the status_OscFreqHz  signal. 

For undamped systems, the frequency is the equivalent to k_NatFreq (ω in the calculations 
above), for under damped systems this set to cal_DampFreqRS (Ω in the calculations above).

Note:    cal_DampFreqRS is a calculated value, calculated internally by the module.

The actual period of oscillation, is given in status_Period and is always in units of seconds.

If the system is non-oscillatory, the signals status_OscFreqRS, status_OscFreqHz  and 
status_Period are all set to zero.

3.4     Understanding the responses


Section 2.3 gives graphical examples of the six types of 2nd order systems responses along with 
the calculation used to generate each type of response (summarised in § 3.2).

In all the examples of section 2.3, the system gain (k_Gain, K in the calculations) is set to 1, 
giving a common scale to the output responses. Setting a different value for k_Gain simply scales 
the results accordingly.

Various rules of thumb for each of the six types of responses are given in section 2.3, these are 
summarised below and where calculated by the module, the associated variable in the 
DYNAMIC_DATA parameter is specified.

                  <Text>版本信息写入。▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂
3.5     Expressing the calculations in Controller operations

The calculations above must be rendered in a form suitable for the Simatic S7-1500 Controller, 
using the mathematical operations available to that Controller, these are listed in Table 2.1.

To perform the calculations in the Controller it will be necessary to use partial calculation to 
hold separate components of the overall calculation and combine these to produce the final 
result. 

The following sections breakdown each of the response calculations into these partial 
calculations and demonstrate how these are then combined to provide a final result that is 
compatible with the Controller mathematical operations and Controller notations.



▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁
3.5.1     Over damped, slow response no overshoot             ζ &gt; 1


CALCULATION:

        ╓   1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t       1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t ╖
y = x K║1 ─ -- │------------------ ┼ 1│ｅ         ┼ -- │------------------ ─ 1│ｅ           ║
     ╙   2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            ╜



Is rendered into the correct format as follows:


 cal_01 = SQRT ( SQR (ζ) - 1)         = √(ζ² ─ 1)

                                 ζ
 cal_02 = ζ ÷ cal_01              = -----------------
                         √(ζ² ─ 1)

 cal_03 = ζ + cal_01              = ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1)

 cal_04 = -1 × ω × t × cal_03           = - ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t

                             -ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t 
 cal_05 = EXP( cal_04 )              =ｅ

 cal_06 = ζ - cal_01               = ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1)

 cal_07 = -1 × ω × t × cal_06           = - ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t

                           -ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t 
 cal_08 = EXP( cal_07 )              =ｅ

                          1 ┌   ζ       ┐
 cal_09 = (cal_02 - 1) × 0.5           = -- │------------------ ─ 1│
                          2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘

                          1 ┌   ζ       ┐
 cal_10 = (cal_02 + 1) × 0.5            = -- │------------------ ┼ 1│
                          2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘

                          1 ┌   ζ       ┐   -ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t
 cal_11 = cal_09 × cal_05             = -- │------------------ ─ 1│ｅ
                          2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘

                          1 ┌   ζ       ┐   -ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t
 cal_12 = cal_10 × cal_08             = -- │------------------ ┼ 1│ｅ
                          2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘

                         ╓   1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t       1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t ╖
 cal_13 = 1 - cal_12 + cal_11             = ║1 ─ -- │------------------ ┼ 1│ｅ         ┼ -- │------------------ ─ 1│ｅ           ║
                         ╙   2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            ╜

                            ╓   1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t       1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t ╖
 OUTPUT  = INPUT x K × cal_13            =  x K║1 ─ -- │------------------ ┼ 1│ｅ         ┼ -- │------------------ ─ 1│ｅ           ║
                            ╙   2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            ╜



▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁
3.5.2     Critically damped, fastest response without overshoot        ζ = 1


CALCULATION:

      ╓       - ωt  ╖
 y = x K║1 ─ (1 ┼ ωt) ｅ    ║
      ╙            ╜


Is rendered into the correct format as follows:


 cal_01 = -1 × ω × t                = - ωt  

                         - ωt
 cal_02 = EXP( cal_01 )              =ｅ

 cal_03 = 1 - cal_01              = 1 ─ (-ωt) = 1 ┼ ωt

                              - ωt
 cal_04 = cal_03 × cal_02            = (1 ┼ ωt) ｅ

                                - ωt
 cal_05 = 1 - cal_04               = 1 ─ (1 ┼ ωt) ｅ

                            ╓          - ωt  ╖
 OUTPUT  = INPUT x K × cal_05            =  x K║1 ─ (1 ┼ ωt) ｅ    ║
                            ╙            ╜



▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁
3.5.3     Under damped, decreasing oscillations              0 &lt; ζ &lt; 1


CALCULATION:

      ╓      - ζω t  ┌        ζ            ┐╖
 y = x K║1 ─ ｅ   │COS (Ωt) ┼ ------------------ SIN (Ωt)│║  where Ω =  ω √(1 ─ ζ²)
      ╙       └       √(1 ─ ζ²)       ┘╜


Is rendered into the correct format as follows:


 cal_01 = SQRT ( 1 - SQR (ζ))         = √(1 ─ ζ²)

                                 ζ
 cal_02 = ζ ÷ cal_01              = -----------------
                         √(1 ─ ζ²)

 cal_03 = ω × cal_01                = ω √(1 ─ ζ²) = Ω

 cal_04 = t × cal_03              = Ωt

 cal_05 = COS( cal_04 )             = COS (Ωt)

 cal_06 = SIN( cal_04 )               = SIN (Ωt)

 cal_07 = -1 × ζ × ω × t             = - ζω t 

                         - ζω t 
 cal_08 = EXP( cal_07 )              =ｅ

                         - ζω t 
 cal_09 = cal_08 × cal_05            =ｅ         COS (Ωt)

 
                                 ζ      - ζω t
 cal_10 = cal_02 × cal_08 × cal_06        = ----------------- ｅ         SIN (Ωt)
                         √(1 ─ ζ²)

                           ╓      - ζω t          ζ     - ζω t            ╖  ╓      - ζω t  ┌        ζ            ┐╖
 cal_11 = 1 - cal_09 - cal_10           =║1 ─ ｅ   COS (Ωt) ─ ------------------ ｅ   SIN (Ωt)║=║1 ─ ｅ   │COS (Ωt) ┼ ------------------ SIN (Ωt)│║
                           ╙              √(1 ─ ζ²)              ╜  ╙       └       √(1 ─ ζ²)       ┘╜

                            ╓      - ζω t  ┌        ζ            ┐╖
 OUTPUT  = INPUT x K × cal_11            =  x K║1 ─ ｅ   │COS (Ωt) ┼ ------------------ SIN (Ωt)│║
                            ╙       └       √(1 ─ ζ²)       ┘╜




▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁
3.5.4     Undamped, oscillates with frequency ω              ζ = 0


CALCULATION:

      ╓       ╖
 y = x K║1 ─ COS (ωt) ║
      ╙       ╜


Is rendered into the correct format as follows:


 cal_01 = ω × t                  = ωt

 cal_02 = COS( cal_01 )             = COS (ωt)

 cal_03 = 1 - cal_02              = 1 ─ COS (ωt) 

 OUTPUT  = INPUT x K × cal_13              =  x K[1 ─ COS (ωt)]



▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁
3.5.5     Unstable, oscillations of increasing amplitude           -1 &lt; ζ &lt; 0


CALCULATION:

 y = x K║1 ─ ｅ   │COS (Ωt) ┼ ------------------ SIN (Ωt)│║  where Ω =  ω √(1 ─ ζ²)
      ╙       └       √(1 ─ ζ²)       ┘╜


Is rendered into the correct format as follows:

                         √(1 ─ ζ²)

 cal_04 = t × cal_03              = Ωt

 cal_05 = COS( cal_04 )             = COS (Ωt)

 cal_06 = SIN( cal_04 )               = SIN (Ωt)

 cal_07 = -1 × ζ × ω × t             = - ζω t

                         √(1 ─ ζ²)

 cal_11 = 1 - cal_09 - cal_10           =║1 ─ ｅ   COS (Ωt) ─ ------------------ ｅ   SIN (Ωt)║=║1 ─ ｅ   │COS (Ωt) ┼ ------------------ SIN (Ωt)│║
                           ╙              √(1 ─ ζ²)              ╜  ╙       └       √(1 ─ ζ²)       ┘╜

     ╙   2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            ╜

3.6     Operating modes


This block FC19512_StdDebugInst2Order supports manual and automatic operating modes, the 
default mode is automatic.

The module can be switched between automatic and manual modes with the 
mode_AutMan signal:

 DATA STRUCTURE    UT39512_Dy_DebugInst2Order
 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
 SIGNAL         FUNCTION               TYPE     DETAILS
 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
 Mode_AutMan     Specifies the operating mode of     Bool  1 = automatic mode
           the simulation                 0 = manual mode

 Mode_ManTime     Specifies the manual time value of       Real     Elapsed time
           the simulation in seconds           in seconds

 status_Aut      The simulation is in automatic mode   Bool  1 = auto mode
                                 0 = not in auto

 status_Man       The simulation is in manual mode    Bool  1 = manual mode
                                 0 = not in manual
 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――  



▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁
3.6.1    Automatic mode


By default the module will be in automatic mode. 

In automatic mode, if the simulation is active (TRIGGER = 1), the module carries out the relevant 
calculation (listed in § 3.2) depending on the value of the damping factor (k_DampFactor) each 
time the module is called. The module calculates the elapsed time based on the current CPU 
time when the module was called, compared with the CPU time when the simulation was 
started (rising edge of TRIGGER) and stored in actual_StartTime.

In automatic mode, a real time simulation occurs, generating responses similar to those shown 
in the plots of § 2.3.  



▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁
3.6.2    Manual mode


In manual mode, if the simulation is active (TRIGGER = 1), the module carries out the relevant 
calculation (listed in § 3.2) depending on the value of the damping factor (k_DampFactor) each 
time the module is called; in exactly the same way as automatic mode.

The difference with manual mode, is that the time used in the calculation must be uniquely 
specified, the elapsed time is not calculated and a manual time value must be provided.

The manual time is given in the variable mode_ManTime and is specified in seconds.

If mode mode_ManTime remains constant between module calls, the module will return the 
same OUTPUT value each time (assuming all other signals remain unchanged).

Manual mode allows the module to calculate the correct response for a particular and exact time, 
and is not dependent on cycle times or other factors that may affect when the module is called.



▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁
3.7      Symbols, block icons and faceplates

There is no supervisory system interface for this block. It is a debug simulation module and as
such has no graphical symbol, block icon or faceplate.

8.     BLOCK CALLS AND ASSOCIATIONS


This section details any blocks which may be called from within this software module (subroutine 
functions for example), any partner blocks with which it may be associated (for example a 
receive module that is partner with a transmit module &amp;c.). It lists any system functions which 
may be called (e.g. reading the real time clock) and any system data types that may be used.

Finally, it lists any special calling requirements for the block (for example, must be called from 
within a cyclic interrupt organisation block) and if the block is using “optimised access” (this is 
the default arrangement).



▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂

There are no PAL block calls from within this block.

 SCR    Source Code Review      A visual inspection of the software to ensure it has been written  
┌┐             to the correct standards, uses the correct structures within the
└┘             software and is generally suitable for deployment.               

 SMT Software Module Test    A full and detailed test of an individual software module in
  ▛▜              isolation; such testing requires that all branches of the 
  ▙▟              software are tested. 

               It tests all the interfaces to the module, any data recorded or 
               stored by the module, all error and exception handling functions 
               and tests all timed and interrupt driven operations.

 SCV Software Compatibility     A mechanism for verifying that no executable code software 
╓╖    Verification          changes have been made to a module following changes to
╙╜             comment fields.

               Allows typographical errors &amp;c. to be corrected without forcing 
               a full SMT on a module that has not functionally changed.
――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――

An SCV can only be performed on a module that has at some point previously, successfully 
completed both an SCR and SMT. Where an SCV is implemented, it replaces the requirement for 
both the SCR and the SMT for the test iteration in question.

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="31" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="32" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>运行时长。
At this point the simulation is running (TRIGGER = 1), read the CPU real time clock and store in the 
working variable act_CPUTime.

This time is then used as the current time for all calculations within the module.
▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
          <MultilingualText ID="33" CompositionName="Title">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="34" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>SIMULATION RUNNING — Read current time</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
        </ObjectList>
      </SW.Blocks.CompileUnit>
      <SW.Blocks.CompileUnit ID="35" CompositionName="CompileUnits">

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="36" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="37" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>转秒。
If the TRIGGER parameter has gone high, and is seen for the first time (status_Running = 0),
THEN a rising edge has been detected on the TRIGGER signal (the simulation has started).

If a rising edge is detected:
  1. Store the current time (act_CPUTime) as the simulation start time (actual_StartTime)
  2. Set the status_Running bit to match the TRIGGER signal
  3. Set the status_Stopped bit to match the inverse of the TRIGGER signal
▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄
</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
          <MultilingualText ID="38" CompositionName="Title">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="39" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>SIMULATION RUNNING — Check for TRIGGER rising edge</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
        </ObjectList>
      </SW.Blocks.CompileUnit>
      <SW.Blocks.CompileUnit ID="3A" CompositionName="CompileUnits">
        <AttributeList>
          <NetworkSource><FlgNet xmlns="http://www.siemens.com/automation/Openness/SW/NetworkSource/FlgNet/v4">

              <MultilingualTextItem ID="3C" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>步长。
If the TRIGGER parameter is high (the simulation is running), then:
Subtract the start time from the current to give the current elapsed time (wrkElapsedTime)
▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>

              <MultilingualTextItem ID="3E" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>SIMULATION RUNNING — Calculate current elapsed time</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
        </ObjectList>

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="40" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="41" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>转秒。
The wrkElapsedTime signal is of data type LTime (a 64-bit number representing the recorded
duration in nanoseconds).

This signal is converted first to a LInt (long integer) and then to a REAL number.

This REAL number is then divided by 1,000,000,000 (1×10^9) to convert the duration from 
nanoseconds to seconds

This final value is returned as actual_RunTime
▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
          <MultilingualText ID="42" CompositionName="Title">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="43" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>SIMULATION RUNNING — Convert elapsed time to a REAL number in seconds</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
        </ObjectList>
      </SW.Blocks.CompileUnit>

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="4A" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="4B" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>阻尼分类:ζ 与 1/0/-1 比较→OverDamp/CritDamp/UnderDamp/Undamped/USUnder/USOver 六类状态位——全部分支的分发器。
The damping factor determines the type of response:
  1.  ζ &gt; 1        Stable over damped (no oscillations)          status_OverDamp
  2.  ζ = 1     Stable critically damped (no oscillations)         status_CritDamp
  3.  0 &lt; ζ &lt; 1  Stable under damped (decaying oscillations)        status_UnderDamp
  4.  ζ = 0     Stable undamped (constant oscillations)      status_Undamped
  5.  -1 &lt; ζ &lt; 0 Unstable under damped (inc. oscillations)       status_USUnder
  6.  ζ ≤ -1       Unstable over damped (asymptotic increase)    status_USOver

The indicated status bit will be set high for the associated damping factor value

For responses 1, 2, 3 and 4, status_Stable will be set high, indicating the response is stable. 
It  will be reset for responses 5 and 6.

For responses 3, 4 and 6, status_Osc will be set high, indicating the response is oscillatory.
It will be reset for responses 1, 2 and 5.
▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄
</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
          <MultilingualText ID="4C" CompositionName="Title">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="4D" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>SIMULATION RUNNING — Determine type of response</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>
        </ObjectList>
      </SW.Blocks.CompileUnit>

                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>阻尼系数规范化:ζ=-1 特殊值处理(数值边界)。
If the damping factor is set to exactly -1.0, the output response can produce and error.

To compensate under these conditions, the damping factor is adjusted to -1.000001, ensuring an
accurate response is produced.

                  <Text>过阻尼解析解:双指数响应——ζ 大于 1 时无振荡,响应由两个实根决定。
Over damped, slow response no overshoot             ζ > 1


CALCULATION:

        ╓   1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t       1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t ╖
y = x K║1 ─ -- │------------------ ┼ 1│ｅ         ┼ -- │------------------ ─ 1│ｅ           ║
     ╙   2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            ╜



Is rendered into the correct format as follows:


 cal_01 = SQRT ( SQR (ζ) - 1)         = √(ζ² ─ 1)

                                 ζ
 cal_02 = ζ ÷ cal_01              = -----------------
                         √(ζ² ─ 1)

 cal_03 = ζ + cal_01              = ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1)

 cal_04 = -1 × ω × t × cal_03           = - ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t

                             -ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t 
 cal_05 = EXP( cal_04 )              =ｅ

 cal_06 = ζ - cal_01               = ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1)

 cal_07 = -1 × ω × t × cal_06           = - ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t

                           -ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t 
 cal_08 = EXP( cal_07 )              =ｅ

                          1 ┌   ζ       ┐
 cal_09 = (cal_02 - 1) × 0.5           = -- │------------------ ─ 1│
                          2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘

                          1 ┌   ζ       ┐
 cal_10 = (cal_02 + 1) × 0.5            = -- │------------------ ┼ 1│
                          2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘

                          1 ┌   ζ       ┐   -ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t
 cal_11 = cal_09 × cal_05             = -- │------------------ ─ 1│ｅ
                          2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘

                          1 ┌   ζ       ┐   -ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t
 cal_12 = cal_10 × cal_08             = -- │------------------ ┼ 1│ｅ
                          2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘

                         ╓   1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t       1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t ╖
 cal_13 = 1 - cal_12 + cal_11             = ║1 ─ -- │------------------ ┼ 1│ｅ         ┼ -- │------------------ ─ 1│ｅ           ║
                         ╙   2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            ╜

                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>临界阻尼解析解:te^(-ωn·t) 形式——ζ=1 的最快无振荡响应。
Critically damped, fastest response without overshoot        ζ = 1


CALCULATION:

      ╓       - ωt  ╖
 y = x K║1 ─ (1 ┼ ωt) ｅ    ║
      ╙            ╜


Is rendered into the correct format as follows:


 cal_01 = -1 × ω × t                = - ωt  

                         - ωt
 cal_02 = EXP( cal_01 )              =ｅ

 cal_03 = 1 - cal_01              = 1 ─ (-ωt) = 1 ┼ ωt

                              - ωt
 cal_04 = cal_03 × cal_02            = (1 ┼ ωt) ｅ

                                - ωt
 cal_05 = 1 - cal_04               = 1 ─ (1 ┼ ωt) ｅ

                            ╓          - ωt  ╖
 OUTPUT  = INPUT x K × cal_05            =  x K║1 ─ (1 ┼ ωt) ｅ    ║
                            ╙            ╜
▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="68" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="69" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>欠阻尼解析解:衰减正弦——含 Cos/Sin/Exp 组合,ζ 在 0~1 之间的标准二阶响应。
Under damped, decreasing oscillations              0 &lt; ζ &lt; 1


CALCULATION:

      ╓      - ζω t  ┌        ζ            ┐╖
 y = x K║1 ─ ｅ   │COS (Ωt) ┼ ------------------ SIN (Ωt)│║  where Ω =  ω √(1 ─ ζ²)
      ╙       └       √(1 ─ ζ²)       ┘╜


Is rendered into the correct format as follows:


 cal_01 = SQRT ( 1 - SQR (ζ))         = √(1 ─ ζ²)

                                 ζ
 cal_02 = ζ ÷ cal_01              = -----------------
                         √(1 ─ ζ²)

 cal_03 = ω × cal_01                = ω √(1 ─ ζ²) = Ω

 cal_04 = t × cal_03              = Ωt

 cal_05 = COS( cal_04 )             = COS (Ωt)

 cal_06 = SIN( cal_04 )               = SIN (Ωt)

 cal_07 = -1 × ζ × ω × t             = - ζω t 

                         - ζω t 
 cal_08 = EXP( cal_07 )              =ｅ

                         - ζω t 
 cal_09 = cal_08 × cal_05            =ｅ         COS (Ωt)

 
                                 ζ      - ζω t
 cal_10 = cal_02 × cal_08 × cal_06        = ----------------- ｅ         SIN (Ωt)
                         √(1 ─ ζ²)

                           ╓      - ζω t          ζ     - ζω t            ╖  ╓      - ζω t  ┌        ζ            ┐╖
 cal_11 = 1 - cal_09 - cal_10           =║1 ─ ｅ   COS (Ωt) ─ ------------------ ｅ   SIN (Ωt)║=║1 ─ ｅ   │COS (Ωt) ┼ ------------------ SIN (Ωt)│║
                           ╙              √(1 ─ ζ²)              ╜  ╙       └       √(1 ─ ζ²)       ┘╜

                            ╓      - ζω t  ┌        ζ            ┐╖
 OUTPUT  = INPUT x K × cal_11            =  x K║1 ─ ｅ   │COS (Ωt) ┼ ------------------ SIN (Ωt)│║
                            ╙       └       √(1 ─ ζ²)       ┘╜

                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>欠阻尼特性:阻尼频率/振荡频率/周期/峰值时间/峰值——控制系统分析的完整参数集。
Under damped, decreasing oscillations              0 &lt; ζ &lt; 1


ANCILLARY CALCULATIONS:

 Damped frequency of oscillation (rad/s)    Ω =  ω √(1 ─ ζ²) = cal_03        cal_DampFreqRS


                       Ω
 Damped frequency of oscillation (Hz)     f =  ------              cal_DampFreqHz
                         2π

                         2π    1
 Damped (actual) period of oscillation (s)    Td =  ------ = ------          cal_Period
                       Ω        f

                                 - ζπ(ω / Ω) 
 Peak overshoot value            Ypk = Kx ┼ Kｅ                cal_PeakValue


                       π    Td
 Time to peak value (s)           Tpk =  ------ = ------          cal_TimePeak
                       Ω       2

                          4
 Time to 98% of steady state value (s)     TSS = ------            cal_TimeSteady
                            ζω

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="72" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="73" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>无阻尼解析解:等幅 Cos 振荡(ζ=0)。
Undamped, oscillates with frequency ω              ζ = 0


CALCULATION:

      ╓       ╖
 y = x K║1 ─ COS (ωt) ║
      ╙       ╜


Is rendered into the correct format as follows:


 cal_01 = ω × t                  = ωt

 cal_02 = COS( cal_01 )             = COS (ωt)

 cal_03 = 1 - cal_02              = 1 ─ COS (ωt) 

 OUTPUT  = INPUT x K × cal_13              =  x K[1 ─ COS (ωt)]

▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>

        <ObjectList>
          <MultilingualText ID="7C" CompositionName="Comment">
            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="7D" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>不稳定欠阻尼:ζ 为负时振幅增长(±87°钳位防数值溢出)。
Unstable, oscillations of increasing amplitude           -1 &lt; ζ &lt; 0


CALCULATION:

        ╓   1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t       1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t ╖
y = x K║1 ─ -- │------------------ ┼ 1│ｅ         ┼ -- │------------------ ─ 1│ｅ           ║
     ╙   2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            ╜



Is rendered into the correct format as follows:


 cal_01 = SQRT ( SQR (ζ) - 1)         = √(ζ² ─ 1)

                                 ζ
 cal_02 = ζ ÷ cal_01              = -----------------
                         √(ζ² ─ 1)

 cal_03 = ζ + cal_01              = ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1)

 cal_04 = -1 × ω × t × cal_03           = - ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t

                             -ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t 
 cal_05 = EXP( cal_04 )              =ｅ

 cal_06 = ζ - cal_01               = ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1)

 cal_07 = -1 × ω × t × cal_06           = - ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t

                           -ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t 
 cal_08 = EXP( cal_07 )              =ｅ

                          1 ┌   ζ       ┐
 cal_09 = (cal_02 - 1) × 0.5           = -- │------------------ ─ 1│
                          2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘

                          1 ┌   ζ       ┐
 cal_10 = (cal_02 + 1) × 0.5            = -- │------------------ ┼ 1│
                          2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘

                          1 ┌   ζ       ┐   -ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t
 cal_11 = cal_09 × cal_05             = -- │------------------ ─ 1│ｅ
                          2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘

                          1 ┌   ζ       ┐   -ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t
 cal_12 = cal_10 × cal_08             = -- │------------------ ┼ 1│ｅ
                          2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘

                         ╓   1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t       1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t ╖
 cal_13 = 1 - cal_12 + cal_11             = ║1 ─ -- │------------------ ┼ 1│ｅ         ┼ -- │------------------ ─ 1│ｅ           ║
                         ╙   2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            ╜

                            ╓   1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t       1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t ╖
 OUTPUT  = INPUT x K × cal_13            =  x K║1 ─ -- │------------------ ┼ 1│ｅ         ┼ -- │------------------ ─ 1│ｅ           ║
                            ╙   2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            ╜
▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁
A note on output limits:

The magnitude of the output will be constrained to the range ±9.9 × 10^±37, this is within
the maximum range of a real number (±3.4 × 10^±38) and is achieved by restricting the 
cal_07 value such that:    -87.0 &lt; cal_07 &lt; 87.0. This in turn restricts the result of the exponential
calculation (cal_08) to the specified range (±9.9 × 10^±37) thus avoiding any mathematical
overflow situation within the CPU.
▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄</Text>
                </AttributeList>
              </MultilingualTextItem>
            </ObjectList>
          </MultilingualText>

            <ObjectList>
              <MultilingualTextItem ID="87" CompositionName="Items">
                <AttributeList>
                  <Culture>en-US</Culture>
                  <Text>不稳定过阻尼:指数发散(9E37 钳位防溢出)——数学上不稳定,工程上警示。
Unstable, unbounded asymptotic increase              ζ ≤ -1


CALCULATION:

        ╓   1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t       1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t ╖
y = x K║1 ─ -- │------------------ ┼ 1│ｅ         ┼ -- │------------------ ─ 1│ｅ           ║
     ╙   2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            ╜



Is rendered into the correct format as follows:


 cal_01 = SQRT ( SQR (ζ) - 1)         = √(ζ² ─ 1)

                                 ζ
 cal_02 = ζ ÷ cal_01              = -----------------
                         √(ζ² ─ 1)

 cal_03 = ζ + cal_01              = ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1)

 cal_04 = -1 × ω × t × cal_03           = - ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t

                             -ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t 
 cal_05 = EXP( cal_04 )              =ｅ

 cal_06 = ζ - cal_01               = ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1)

 cal_07 = -1 × ω × t × cal_06           = - ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t

                           -ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t 
 cal_08 = EXP( cal_07 )              =ｅ

                          1 ┌   ζ       ┐
 cal_09 = (cal_02 - 1) × 0.5           = -- │------------------ ─ 1│
                          2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘

                          1 ┌   ζ       ┐
 cal_10 = (cal_02 + 1) × 0.5            = -- │------------------ ┼ 1│
                          2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘

                          1 ┌   ζ       ┐   -ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t
 cal_11 = cal_09 × cal_05             = -- │------------------ ─ 1│ｅ
                          2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘

                          1 ┌   ζ       ┐   -ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t
 cal_12 = cal_10 × cal_08             = -- │------------------ ┼ 1│ｅ
                          2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘

                         ╓   1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t       1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t ╖
 cal_13 = 1 - cal_12 + cal_11             = ║1 ─ -- │------------------ ┼ 1│ｅ         ┼ -- │------------------ ─ 1│ｅ           ║
                         ╙   2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            ╜

                            ╓   1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ─ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t       1 ┌   ζ       ┐   - ω [ ζ ┼ √(ζ² ─ 1) ]t ╖
 OUTPUT  = INPUT x K × cal_13            =  x K║1 ─ -- │------------------ ┼ 1│ｅ         ┼ -- │------------------ ─ 1│ｅ           ║
                            ╙   2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            2 └ √(ζ² ─ 1)     ┘            ╜
▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁
A note on output limits:

The magnitude of the output will be constrained to the limit 9.0 × 10^37, this is within
the maximum range of a real number (±3.4 × 10^±38) and is achieved by 
setting the output to a value of 9.0 × 10^37 if either cal_04 or cal_04 are outside
the range  -87.0 &lt; cal_04/7 &lt; 87.0.

This may cause an irregularity in the output at the point at which this condition is reached, the 
output will jump to the value 9.0 × 10^37 whenever cal_04 or cal_07 reaches the value of 87.0. 

This is not considered significant given the unstable nature of the response and the very large 
numbers involved.
▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄</Text>
                </AttributeList>

TITLE:    GENERAL — EXAMPLE DOCUMENTATION

FC61000_DocGenExample is a documentation block that contains examples of all the typical 
forms of documentation used within the PAL.

The block is intended to be an easy reference area that allows the various forms of 
documentation to be cut and pasted into new blocks.

All the examples are based on the instructions contained within the Style Guide 
document [Ref. 009], available here: https://psop.uk/pal-sg-p.

The block itself does not do anything (it has no executable code other than that for hardcoding 
the revision and licence information); and should not be called. Its purpose is purely to store 
examples of the documentation and styles used in networks and comment areas within the 
PAL software.

2.     FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTION


FC61000 is the Example Documentation block, it is a documentation module that contains 
examples of all the common block and network comments used throughout the PAL software.

All examples are based upon the Style Guide [Ref. 009], available here:
     https://psop.uk/pal-sg-p

The examples are intended to be a common resource when developing software using the PAL 
software; acting as quick reference points to be used for all the common stylistic arrangements 
used when documenting software within the PAL.

The module is divided into different networks, with the comments for each network explaining 
and giving examples of a particular aspect of comment styles (headings, body text, tables, 
figures &amp;c.).

Additional networks containing a full list of the common characters available to the 
Siemens TIA font (this being the font used within all comment sections) are provided.


CONTENTS (BY NETWORK)

NW 1.    Block description — Sections 1 to 3.2 (this network)
NW 2.    Block description — Sections 3.3 to 3.4
NW 3.    Block description — Sections 3.5 to 10
NW 4.    Current revision and modification history


WORKED EXAMPLES

NW 5.    Example — OB1 NETWORK 1  — Project description
NW 6.    Example — OB1 NETWORK 2  — Project revision and modification history
NW 7.    Example — BLOCK LEVEL       — Block description — Sections 1 to 10
NW 8.    Example — BLOCK LEVEL       — Current revision and modification history


COMMENT STRUCTURE EXAMPLES

NW 9.    Example — Headings, lists and indented text
NW 10.    Example — Body text
NW 11.    Example — Standard Tables
NW 12.    Example — Other tables
NW 13.    Example — Equations
NW 14.    Example — Figures


CHARACTER LISTS

NW 15.    Special characters — Hyphens, whitespace and construction lines
NW 16.    Special characters — Arrows, box and block characters
NW 17.    Special characters — Currency, punctuation and full-width and small characters
NW 18.    Special characters — Greek, indexing characters and Roman numerals
NW 19.    Special characters — Mathematical operators (including vulgar fractions)
NW 20.    Special characters — Geometrical and ornamental characters
NW 21.    Special characters — Common character widths and additional whitespace characters


TYPICAL NETWORK COMMENTS

NW 22.    Load the system RTC and store in local variable  [typical network comment]
NW 23.    ██ STEP 03340 — DECLARATION (RUNNING)    [sequence network comment]
NW 24.       STEP 03340 — ACTION (INITIALISE)           [sequence network comment]
NW 25.       STEP 03340 — TRANSITION 01                   [sequence network comment]
NW 26.   LICENCE AND CONTACT INFORMATION       [final network]


This documentation module (FC61000) itself does not contain any executable code. With the 
exception of the revision and licence networks, all networks are empty. The block itself does

▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄▄
3.     DETAILED BLOCK DESCRIPTION


The purpose of this block is to provide an easy point of reference for the various documentation 
constructs and styles used within the PAL.

The contents of this block are extracts from the Style Guide [Ref. 009], available here:
     https://psop.uk/pal-sg-p

The block itself does not contain any executable code, with the exception of the revision and 
licence networks, all networks are empty. The block itself does nothing, and its execution will 
have no effect, other than extending the cycle time.

The block provides examples of all the common structures and styles used in the Block 
description, Current revision and all network comment areas. The examples are split into 
separate networks (see "Contents by network" above).

All block documentation created using TIA Portal, is stored in the various comment fields 
available to a block (there is a comment field associated with the block title area and each 
network within the block has its own comment field; additionally, each network has its own title 
line as does the block itself).

These comment fields are not particularly sophisticated and cannot be customised; they use a 
fixed font at non-adjustable point size. The font in question is Siemens TIA Portal Basic and it 
uses a fixed-point size of 9 pt. that cannot be changed.

A comment field for any network can hold approximately 65000 characters including spaces and 
line break characters.

This equates to approximately 670 lines of text, and with (a typical) 19.2 words per line, this is in 
the region of 13,000 words per comment field (per network). 



▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂
3.1     Conventions and common terminology



▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂
3.1.1     Common PAL abbreviations


There are four common types of blocks associated with Siemens Controllers, three 
programmable blocks (functions, function blocks and organisation blocks), and global data 
storage blocks (data blocks). There are also instance data blocks that hold information for 
specific function blocks. Finally, the PAL treats User Data Types as blocks (UDTs are not blocks, 
but the PAL always associates then with a specific block and names them accordingly).

Each of these block types (and the UDTs) is given a two-letter abbreviation that uniquely identifies 
its type within the software:


 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
 BLOCK ABBREVIATION    MEANING
 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
 FB              Function block
 FC              Function
 OB             Organisation block
 DB             Data block
 ID              Instance data block
 UT              User data type
 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――
 Table 3.1   Block type abbreviations


All block names (and UDT names) will start with one of these block identifier abbreviations:

Within the PAL all blocks (and UDTs) are given a name; that name has a particular structure that 
includes the block identifier (above), the block number (address), a block class, a block function 
attribute and a description formatted as follows:

 ｎｎｎｎｎ    Block number       5 digits (in the range 00000-61000)
 Ｃｃｃ      Block class         3 characters (see block class below) 
 Ｆｆｆｆｆｆ   Block function       5 characters max (see block function below)

Block description


The block description (Ｄｄｄｄｄｄｄｄ) does not have a prescribed list of naming options; 
it is simply a short form description of what the block does. Examples are:


 ――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――――

Block descriptions are always written without spaces using camel case¹ ; typically, block 
descriptions should be 12 characters or fewer in length.


――――――――――
¹         Camel case is the practice of joining words together and capitalising the start of each 
     word, it is more formal known as medial capitals.
――――――――――



▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂
3.1.3     Block naming restrictions


The basic restrictions on naming blocks within the PAL are:

   1. The Class abbreviation is three characters long and starts with a capital letter

   2. The Function abbreviation is no more than five characters long and must start with a 
     capital letter

   3. The Description does not have a restriction on the number of characters but should 
     generally be kept short

   4. Each separate word in the description is capitalised with all other letters in lowercase 
     (this includes the first word)

   5. The overall length of the name (including class, function and description) must be 
     20 characters or less

   6. Only the characters [a-z], [A-Z], the numbers [0-9], the dash/hyphen [-] and the 
     underscore [ _ ] are permitted



▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂
3.1.4     General abbreviations and conventions


Abbreviations are always capitalised except where there is an accepted convention or 
manufacturer’s trade mark (such as AS-i).

This document uses the capitalisation of nouns to indicate elements of the control system and 
its associated equipment, for example Control System refers to the control system being 
programmed (rather than a nonspecific control system used as a general reference). 
Similarly, Controller refers to a Siemens S7-1200/1500 controller.



▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂
3.2     Common settings



TIA Portal is a highly configurable package and its appearance can be drastically changed by 
reconfiguring the package settings.

TIA Portal settings are split into two types: Project specific settings that apply only to the current 
project (this covers languages &amp;c.), and global settings that are configured for the package as 
a whole and that apply to every project that is loaded (things like font size, colours, display 
arrangements &amp;c.).

Some properties within TIA Portal are dependent on the underlying Windows operating system 
settings (specifically date and time formats used within TIA Portal) and to give a common look 
and feel to projects within TIA Portal, these should be changed too.

Finally, the PAL requires certain settings and configurations to be applied to whichever 
processor (CPU) is to be used to run the PAL software.

The content here is a subset of that contained in the ES/WDP Configuration Manual [Ref. 010], 
available here:

     https://psop.uk/pal-es-p



▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂
3.2.1     Windows regional settings


TIA Portal is not responsive to the regional settings selected within windows¹. TIA Portal only 
uses the REGION AND LANGUAGE settings for ENGLISH (UNITED STATES). 

Where other regions are used — ENGLISH (UNITED KINGDOM) for example, then TIA Portal will 
ignore this and use the default setting for ENGLISH (UNITED STATES). This tends to mean that 
dates always default to the American format of mm/dd/yyyy, and this is generally not acceptable.

The only way to change this is to set the region and language to ENGLISH (UNITED STATES) and 
then change the defaults to something more English (British) in nature.

With Windows 10/11, the region settings can be accessed by clicking the WINDOWS START button 
and entering region. It will appear at the top of the search list (as region, control panel). Click it 
and then select additional settings.

In the first tab (NUMBERS) change the measurement system to METRIC.

In the second tab (CURRENCY change the currency to £ — just overtype the dollar sign, the 
dropdown does not show the £ sign).

In the TIME tab, select the SHORT and LONG times to have two capital H characters at the start. 
This causes time to be displayed in the 24-hour clock format with leading zeros to make sure 
the hours always occupy two characters (e.g. 01:08 instead of 1:08 AM):

     SHORT TIME:    HH:mm
     LONG TIME:     HH:mm:ss

The date tab must be set to use an unambiguous date format (the dd/mm/yyyy and mm/dd/yyyy 
used respectively by the British and Americans can lead to confusion with days numbered less 
than 13 e.g. 12/01/2019 could be read as 12 January 2019 or 01 December 2019). 

The acceptable formats for dates are either specifying the month with letters (Jan, Feb, 
Mar &amp;c.) or by using the ISO 8601 [Ref. 101] standard date format (this is generally the 
preferred format within engineering projects ).

     SHORT DATE:      yyyy-MM-dd
     LONG DATE:       dd MMM yyyy
     SHORT TIME:    HH:mm
     LONG TIME:     HH:mm:ss


――――――――――
¹         This is an omission on the part of TIA Portal, all Windows programmes should adopt 
     the region settings selected by Windows — it is however consistent with earlier 
     versions of Siemens programming packages: Simatic Manager (Step 7) and PCS 7; 
     both of which ignored the Windows regional settings. 
――――――――――



▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂▂
3.2.2     TIA Portal restoring default settings


To provide a common interface format, the PAL uses the default settings for TIA Portal as much 
as possible. However, there are a few areas where these settings need to be changed to match 
the requirements of the PAL.

To start from a common point, the TIA Portal settings should be restored to their default values. 
This is done under the settings menu: select OPTIONS → SETTINGS. To opens the main settings 
window in the central display area:

Firstly, ensure that the USER INTERFACE LANGUAGE is set to ENGLISH

There are three RESET TO DEFAULT buttons in the second row down. The first button 
ALL APPLICATION SETTINGS restores all the settings within the application and for all the editor 
types back to their default values, it also restores all the editor layouts back to their default 
arrangements and re-activates any messages that may have been suppressed.

The second button EDITOR LAYOUTS just restores the screen arrangements back to their 
default configurations (the first button also does this, but this button does not restore any 
other application settings).

The third button SHOW ALL MESSAGE WINDOWS, resets any pop-up messages that have been 
disabled (by clicking the DO NOT SHOW THIS MESSAGE AGAIN option) so that they will be 
shown once more if the necessary conditions to trigger them occur.

To restore the default settings, click the first button: ALL APPLICATION SETTINGS (this is effectively 
the same as clicking the second and third buttons too since it resets the window layouts and 
any messages that have been suppressed).

TIA Portal must be closed and reopened for the changes to take effect. 
――――――――――
